Section 2.2 says habit changes only for a significantly more satisfying and less dissonant choice; Appendix A's procedure compares dissonance only when satisfaction is within threshold.
Appendix A does not specify dissonance behavior when positive and negative evaluation sums are both zero.
The framework permits case-specific network tie changes but does not provide a generic tie-update rule.
Section 2's exchange activation criterion conflicts with Appendix A's positive singular dissonance-strength gate.
Section 2's social-importance threshold conflicts with Appendix A's linear rescaling/sign criterion.
Appendix A ranks the full cached alter list but leaves explicit filtering and exhausted-list behavior unspecified.
Table 1 describes singular dissonance-strength as that of the chosen alternative, while Table 2 stores per-alternative strengths without stating synchronization after choice changes.
Signal item 30 is defined as the sum of items 25–30 including item 30 itself; intended aggregation is unresolved.
